summary: 80-byte worker-thread wrapper: kernel thread at +0x04 (handle +0x04, joined flag +0x08), a 0x1000-byte stack buffer at +0x10/+0x14 and an embedded virtual callback (vtable +0x44, owner +0x48, argument +0x4C) invoked by thread entry 0x001150DC. Destroyed by Os_ThreadObject_Dtor (0x005761D8); the class name is a legacy M1 label.
evidence: Ctor 0x001D0134 stores self at +0x48, self+0x44 at +0xC and its second argument at +0x4C, then starts a thread through 0x0010EAB0 (0x1000-byte stack, priority 0x10). Thread entry 0x001150DC does p=[self+0xC]; (*p)->slot2(p), i.e. +0x0C points at the embedded callback starting at +0x44.

fields.name: callback
fields.evidence: Ctor 0x001D0134: *(int *)(param_1 + 0xc) = param_1 + 0x44; thread entry 0x001150DC loads [self+0xC] and calls the object's virtual slot 2, so this is the pointer to the embedded callback at +0x44.

fields.name: callbackVtable
fields.evidence: First word of the embedded callback at +0x44; 0x001150DC reads [self+0xC] then [that]=this word and branches to [it+8] (virtual slot 2). Not written by the base init, so the derived ctor installs it.

fields.name: callbackOwner
fields.evidence: Ctor 0x001D0134: *(int *)(param_1 + 0x48) = param_1; the callback object at +0x44 keeps a back-pointer to the thread wrapper that owns it.

fields.name: callbackArg
fields.evidence: Ctor 0x001D0134: *(undefined4 *)(param_1 + 0x4c) = param_2; Fs_FileRequest_Update (0x0032F5BC) passes its outer file-request object here, so this is the argument handed to the thread callback.

summary: Destructor view of the 80-byte worker-thread wrapper also described as Os_SyncObject: installs vtable 0x00782668, joins the kernel thread and closes the handle at +0x04 (svc #0x23), then releases the stack buffer via 0x0010EA00. 'CriticalSection' is a legacy M1 name: this is a thread object.
evidence: 0x005761D8 stores 0x00782668 (= asm/rodata 0x00782668, slot 0 = 0x005761D8 itself) at +0, calls 0x0010EA00(self) (frees the stack buffer at +0x10/+0x14), joins self+4 via 0x00118170, then svc #0x23 and clears +0x04. Same layout as the object initialised by 0x001D0134.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: *param_1 = DAT_0057621c (0x00782668) in the destructor 0x005761D8; rodata at 0x00782668 holds 0x005761D8 as its first slot.

fields.name: threadHandle
fields.evidence: Destructor 0x005761D8: piVar1 = self+1 (byte +0x04); svc #0x23 (svcCloseHandle) then *piVar1 = 0. 0x0010EA00 also tests the same word and closes it, so it is the kernel thread handle.

summary: 892-byte lazily created global heap/allocator manager (getter 0x001D0170): vtable at +0x00, seven 0x30-byte size-class pool nodes at +0x04..+0x153 (vtable 0x007824D0, slot 0 = Mem_SmallBlockAllocChunk), a 0x007821C8 table at +0x154 with 5x0x10 records, list headers to +0x374; the embedded heap at +0x33C is returned by 0x001D0170.
evidence: Real entry is 0x001064D4: Ghidra started at +4 and dropped 'ldr r1,[pc]=0x0075C310; str r1,[r0],#4'. The ctor chains 7 nodes of 0x30 from self+4 via 0x00109558 (vtable 0x007824D0 at +0, 0x007821B8 at +8), stores 0x007821C8 at +0x154, builds 5x0x10 records at +0x158/+0x1D4, sets list headers up to +0x374, ends at 0x106720. Getter 0x001D0170 allocates 0x37C bytes and returns self+0x33C.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Function entry 0x001064D4: ldr r1,[pc,#0x248] (=0x0075C310); str r1,[r0],#4 stores it at +0 before the pools are built. 0x0075C310 is a table of code pointers (0x00101A9F, 0x00220948, 0x0022616C, ...), i.e. the object's method table.

summary: 176-byte named entry (label "SequenceTask") in the engine's global Container name map: two intrusive list anchors, an embedded rb-tree key node with an FNV-1a name hash and 32-char name, its own name string and a few state bytes. Created by Fs_Task_Create (0x00107F84), freed by the dtor at 0x002598B4.
evidence: Ctor 0x0010673C installs 0x007824E0 then 0x0075CACC at +0, builds two 3-word list anchors (+0x04/+0x10), an rb-tree node at +0x1C (parent/left/right/colour), FNV-1a seed 0x811C9DC5 at +0x30 and the literal "SequenceTask" at +0x64. Fs_Task_Create hashes the name with 0x811C9DC5*0x01000193, inserts the node at +0x1C via std__Rb_tree_insert_and_rebalance and stores the Container at +0x5C.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ctor 0x0010673C writes 0x007824E0 and finally 0x0075CACC here; dtor 0x002598B4 re-stores 0x007824E0; Fs_Task_Create (0x00107F84) calls (**(code **)(*obj + 8))(obj).

fields.name: list1Owner
fields.evidence: Ctor: param_1[1] = param_1. Dtor 0x002598B4 unlinks the anchor whose links are at +0x08/+0x0C and whose owner word is +0x04.

fields.name: list1Next
fields.evidence: Ctor: param_1[2] = param_1 + 1 (empty circular list). Dtor: *(next+8) = prev, i.e. +0x08 is the forward link of the +0x04 anchor.

fields.name: list1Prev
fields.evidence: Ctor: param_1[3] = param_1 + 1. Dtor: *(prev+4) = next, i.e. +0x0C is the backward link of the +0x04 anchor.

fields.name: list2Owner
fields.evidence: Ctor: param_1[4] = param_1. Second intrusive list anchor; dtor unlinks its links at +0x14/+0x18.

fields.name: list2Next
fields.evidence: Ctor: param_1[5] = param_1 + 4 (i.e. &anchor at +0x10). Dtor: *(self[5] + 8) = self[6].

fields.name: list2Prev
fields.evidence: Ctor: param_1[6] = param_1 + 4. Dtor: *(self[6] + 4) = self[5], the backward link of the +0x10 anchor.

fields.name: maybe_treeLink
fields.evidence: Ctor: param_1[7] = param_1 + 7 (self-referential). First word of the embedded rb-tree node used as the Container name-map key; std__Rb_tree_insert_and_rebalance treats +0x1C as the node base (x).

fields.name: treeParent
fields.evidence: Ctor: param_1[8] = &node. std_RbTree_EraseNode documents node+4 = parent; the node base is +0x1C, so parent is +0x20.

fields.name: treeLeft
fields.evidence: Ctor: param_1[9] = &node. std_RbTree_EraseNode: node+8 = left child; node base +0x1C -> +0x24.

fields.name: treeRight
fields.evidence: Ctor: param_1[10] = &node. std_RbTree_EraseNode: node+0xC = right child; node base +0x1C -> +0x28.

fields.name: treeColor
fields.evidence: Ctor: *(undefined1 *)(param_1 + 0xb) = 0. std_RbTree_EraseNode: colour byte at node+0x10; node base +0x1C -> +0x2C.

fields.name: mapKeyHash
fields.evidence: Ctor stores FNV-1a offset basis 0x811C9DC5 at +0x30; Fs_Task_Create recomputes hash = hash*0x01000193 ^ name[i] and Container_NameMap_FindNodePair compares node+0x14 (=+0x30) with the key hash.

summary: 400-byte sound work queue: submit ring at +0x00 (used indirectly), completion ring at +0xB4, pending-node list at +0x16C/+0x170 and a monotone sequence counter at +0x174. Os_WorkQueue_Push (0x00114E60) queues 4-word nodes {next, state, sequence, previous-sequence}; Drain (0x00114FAC) folds completions back.
evidence: Os_WorkQueue_Push calls Os_QueueTryPush(q, q->f_16C) on the ring at +0x00 and Os_QueueTryPop(&q->f_b4,...) on the completion ring; its 4-word node (heap 0x0011B8C0) gets node[3]=f_184 and node[8]=sequence, then q->f_174++. Drain pops the completion ring, copies node[8] to f_178 and the chain tail's node[3] to f_188; callers are Snd_QueueWaveCommand and Sound_Stream_SubmitDmaCommand.

fields.name: completionQueueBuffer
fields.evidence: Os_QueueTryPop(&q->f_b4, &local) in Os_WorkQueue_Push/Drain treats +0xB4 as the base of an embedded OsQueue; the first word of that ring object is its buffer pointer (Os_QueueTryPop reads *(u32*)*queue).

fields.name: pendingHead
fields.evidence: Os_WorkQueue_Push: if (q->f_16c == 0) { alloc node; if (q->f_170 == 0) q->f_16c = node; ... } - head of the list of pending node allocations.

fields.name: pendingTail
fields.evidence: Os_WorkQueue_Push: *q->f_170 = node; q->f_170 = node; *node = 0 - tail pointer of the same pending list.

fields.name: nextSequence
fields.evidence: Os_WorkQueue_Push: result = q->f_174 (returned to the caller as the work sequence), then q->f_174 = q->f_174 + 1.

fields.name: completedSequence
fields.evidence: Os_WorkQueue_Drain: q->f_178 = local_10[2] after Os_QueueTryPop - i.e. the sequence word (node+8) of the completion just popped.

fields.name: inFlightSequence
fields.evidence: Os_WorkQueue_Push stamps the new node with q->f_184 (puVar1[3] = q->f_184) before linking; Drain compares the drained node's predecessor id with q->f_184 to decide whether to roll the tracking back to 0.

fields.name: maybe_previousSequence
fields.evidence: Os_WorkQueue_Drain: q->f_188 = tailNode[3] (the previous-sequence value stored by Push), then q->f_18c = 0; when it equals f_184 both are reset to 0.

fields.name: maybe_pendingRollback
fields.evidence: Os_WorkQueue_Push/Drain always clear this byte to 0 together with the f_188 rollback value (*(undefined1 *)(param_1 + 0x18c) = 0); it is only ever seen cleared.

summary: 24-byte holder for one 3DS kernel object handle at +0x14; embedded in the Fs worker's per-queue state (Fs_Worker_Dtor calls it at self+0x800) and closed by Os_Handle_CloseField (0x006E75A0) with svc #0x23, which clears +0x14.
evidence: Os_Handle_CloseField (0x006E75A0): if (*(int *)(param_1 + 0x14) != 0) { svc #0x23 (svcCloseHandle); *(u32*)(param_1 + 0x14) = 0; } return param_1. Sole caller Fs_Worker_Dtor (0x0056FF4C) passes self+0x800 and self-relative queue pointers; size 24 comes from the batch.

fields.name: kernelHandle
fields.evidence: Os_Handle_CloseField: nonzero -> software_interrupt(0x23) (svcCloseHandle) -> store 0; a 3DS kernel handle stored as u32.
